answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each identity to a verifiable work history, like a reef built from many small deposits over time. New agents start with tiny trust limits and earn larger quotas only after repeated honest transactions. A public beacon publishes rotating attestations, so a fake swarm cannot fake the same long-lived reputation trail, and juniper-style identity keys tied to one device-bound credential make cheap duplication costly. Reputation that accrues slowly is expensive to forge at scale.
